record.paper_title: A collection of open problems in celebration of Imre Leader’s 60th birthday
record.context_brief: Transition point between log-log and log regimes
record.original_question: In the same partial-shattering problem for permutations, for which values of t does the threshold occur at which the minimum size of a family that t-shatters every k-subset of [n] changes from order Θ(log log n) to order Θ(log n)?

evidence.quote: In particular, we have the following questions: • If not, then for which t does the transition from Θ(log log n) to Θ(log n) occur?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For positive integers n and k with k ≤ n, and an integer t with 1 ≤ t ≤ k!, say that a family F of permutations of [n] = {1,2,…,n} t-shatters a k-subset S ⊆ [n] if the restrictions of the permutations in F to S, regarded as linear orderings of S, realize at least t of the k! possible orderings of S. Let f_k(n,t) denote the minimum size of a family F of permutations of [n] that t-shatters every k-subset of [n].

It is known that as n → ∞ (with k and t fixed), f_k(n,t) falls into one of a small number of asymptotic regimes, the largest of which is Θ(log n) and a smaller one of which is Θ(log log n).

Determine all pairs (k, t) for which the threshold transition between the Θ(log log n) regime and the Θ(log n) regime in f_k(n, t) occurs; that is, characterize precisely the values of t (as a function of k) at which f_k(n,t) jumps from order Θ(log log n) to order Θ(log n).
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work by Girão and collaborators (2024) shows that, contrary to earlier expectations, f_k(n,t) admits a fourth asymptotic regime of order Θ(√log n) for some parameters with k ≥ 4, in addition to the Θ(1), Θ(log log n), and Θ(log n) regimes. They establish that f_k(n,t) = Θ(log n) when t > 2^{k-1}, narrowing the range of unresolved (k,t). The exact location of the transition from Θ(log log n) to Θ(log n) is not fully determined for all k and t, so the question is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Small families of partially shattering permutations
status_evidence.snippet: A fourth regime Θ(√log n) is shown to exist for k ≥ 4; for t > 2^{k-1}, f_k(n,t) = Θ(log n).
status_evidence.claim: The threshold question is partially resolved: a new √log n regime is identified and the Θ(log n) regime is established for t > 2^{k-1}.

status_evidence.title: Shattering k-sets with Permutations
status_evidence.snippet: For k = 3 three regimes Θ(1), Θ(log log n), Θ(log n) cover all t; for larger k, regimes may not cover all values of t.
status_evidence.claim: The full characterization of the transition point was previously open beyond k = 3.
